claims.text: Pulumi has a provider support policy that defines how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version and which providers receive long-term security updates.
A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ describing Pulumi's provider support policy.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
Pulumi maintains a published provider support policy page that lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi providers receive no patches at all.
The current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi can be found in the Pulumi Registry.
A page titled 'Provider support policy' exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/.
When a major version of a Pulumi provider is released, that is a signal to begin planning a provider version update.
Major versions of Pulumi providers typically include significant changes such as deprecations, new resources, and new functionality that may require additional migration steps.
Pulumi recommends updating to the latest minor version on the current major provider version at least quarterly.
Minor versions of Pulumi providers typically include new resources and features, as well as performance improvements and bug fixes, without introducing breaking changes.
Patch versions of Pulumi providers are primarily for bug fixes and security updates and are designed to be fully backward compatible.
The npm tilde operator (e.g. ~1.2.3) can be used to allow patch updates on the current minor version.
Users should never be 2 major versions behind on a Pulumi provider, because jumping multiple major versions risks a significant number of breaking changes.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
There is a current, specific list of providers that receive long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi AWS provider receives long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi Azure Classic provider receives long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi Azure Native provider receives long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi Azure AD provider receives long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi Command provider receives long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi Docker Build provider receives long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi GCP provider receives long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider receives long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi TLS provider receives long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi Vault provider receives long-term support updates on eligible older versions.
The Pulumi LTS branch ships fixes for High/Critical CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
The Pulumi LTS branch ships fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship CVE security patches.
An LTS release from Pulumi does not contain new upstream API versions.
An LTS release from Pulumi does not contain new resources or new resource properties.
An LTS release from Pulumi does not contain performance improvements.
An LTS release from Pulumi does not contain non-security bug fixes.
An LTS release from Pulumi does not contain compatibility updates for newer versions of language runtimes.
Pulumi providers are compatible with the version of the Pulumi engine they were frozen at unless otherwise prompted via security fixes.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per Pulumi provider at any time.
Under Pulumi's provider support policy, when major version N+1 ships, it becomes the new current major (N), and the old current major (N) becomes the new long-term support major.
Under Pulumi's provider support policy, when a new major version ships, the old long-term support major reaches end of life on the same day, regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within a Pulumi provider's long-term support major version, only the latest minor version receives patches, and earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases, but are tagged differently.
Pulumi customers pinning to a specific major version will automatically receive patch releases as they ship.
Pinning to a specific major version of a Pulumi provider is the recommended approach.
At any time, exactly one major version of a covered Pulumi provider is the long-term support (LTS) version, and older major versions receive no patches.

Under Pulumi's provider support policy, the current major version (N) of a provider receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.

Under Pulumi's provider support policy, the long-term support major version (N−1) of a provider receives security updates in the provider's code or its direct dependencies for up to 12 months from N's release, or until N+1 ships.
Under Pulumi's provider support policy, provider major versions at end of life (N−2 and older) are not supported and will not receive updates.
